LESSON: READING 14.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.2: Reading 14.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 14.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 14 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: How can we tell that someone has understood a story? 2. What helps us to understand a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 14.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and Imagination: as the learner practices making connections as they talk about their own experiences in relation to the story.

Values:
• Unity: Cooperation is enhanced as they work collaboratively in groups.

• Respect: Love is enhanced as the learner appreciates other’s opinions during group activities.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Creative and critical thinking skills are enhanced as the learner uses analytical skills to make predictions.

English

Link to other Learning Areas:

Kiswahili Language Activities as learners reads and respond to direct and indirect questions from a text to show comprehension.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Pictures, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners,

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
